section.title: Introduction
section.para: The package opennlp.tools.pii finds personally identifiable mentions as exact spans over the original text. A PiiAnnotator writes the opennlp:pii layer from a PiiExtractor; the built-in CursorPiiExtractor recognizes email addresses, phone numbers, IBANs, and payment card numbers, each with a type constant and a normalized form. IBANs and card numbers are checksum validated. Phone candidates use formatting and length checks. An IBAN candidate must also match the ISO 13616 registry: a registered country code and exactly the length that country assigns, so a checksum-passing run with an unknown country or a wrong length is not reported. Email domains must end in an IANA-registered top-level domain (including punycode forms) and stay within the RFC 1035 presentation-length limit, so private-use suffixes such as .internal or .local are not reported. The ASCII local part is capped at 64 characters and the complete mailbox at 254 characters. Local-part case is preserved in the normalized form, while the case-insensitive domain is lowercased. The baked IANA snapshot is refreshed with dev/fetch-iana-tlds.sh; pass --check in an automated drift check without changing the source tree. The calling-code and IBAN length tables are regenerated from libphonenumber and the SWIFT registry with dev/fetch-phone-number-lengths.sh and dev/fetch-iban-lengths.sh, respectively. See Reference data for offline phone-table generation and validation. An extractor limited to a subset of the types, for a caller that wants only payment data found, is built with new CursorPiiExtractor(Set.of(PiiMention.TYPE_CARD)). A type set must be non-null and non-empty, with no null or unrecognized entries; invalid selections raise IllegalArgumentException. Each configurable detector copies the selection, so changing the supplied set after construction does not change its enabled types.

Further detectors, for network addresses, credentials, cryptocurrency addresses, bank routing numbers, national identifiers, and device identifiers, are opt-in and described under Opt-in detectors and packs. None of them is part of CursorPiiExtractor, so what a caller already redacts never changes when a detector is added.

section.title: Annotating and masking
section.para:
A MaskPolicy controls how the covered characters are replaced while staying length preserving. keepingFormat() leaves separators visible so the kind of value stays recognizable, and keepingTrailing(4) leaves the last four letters or digits of each span readable, the customary receipt style. PiiUsageExampleTest asserts the exact output shown here.
String receipt = Masker.mask(document, PiiAnnotator.PII, MaskPolicy.of('*').keepingFormat().keepingTrailing(4)); // "Contact ****@******e.com, call (***) ***-4567, or charge card **** **** **** 1111."

What is customary differs by type, and MaskPolicies collects those defaults: a card keeps its last four digits, an address or an IP address keeps only its separators, and a credential is masked whole, formatting included, since even its shape says which system it opens. Passing the defaults to Masker chooses a policy per mention, so one pass redacts a mixed document correctly.
String masked = Masker.mask(document, PiiAnnotator.PII, MaskPolicies.byType()); // "Contact ****@*******.***, call (***) ***-****, or charge card **** **** **** 1111."

section.title: Opt-in detectors and packs
section.para: CursorPiiExtractor reports email addresses, phone numbers, IBANs, and payment card numbers, and it always will: adding a type to it would silently change what every existing caller redacts. Everything else is opt-in, in extractors that each validate against the standard they implement rather than against a shape.

listitem.para:
NetworkPiiExtractor: IPv4, IPv6, and MAC addresses. It rejects matches inside longer dotted names and numeric values, including Unicode continuations. Trailing IPv6 :: is retained before brackets, whitespace and sentence punctuation. The unspecified IPv4/IPv6 addresses, limited IPv4 broadcast address, and all-zero or broadcast MAC addresses are excluded. IPv6 without an embedded IPv4 part must spell out at least two groups and either spell out all eight groups or include a group of at least three digits. This false-positive filter omits some valid short forms, including ::1 and 2001::. Normalization uses lowercase hexadecimal IPv6 with the first longest run of at least two zero groups compressed, and lowercase colon-separated MAC pairs. Matching does not check assignment or reachability.
Document addresses = new PiiAnnotator(PiiPacks.network()).annotate(Document.of( "Peer [2001:db8::], host 192.0.2.1, MAC 02-1B-44-11-3A-B7.")); String masked = Masker.mask(addresses, PiiAnnotator.PII, '*'); // "Peer [**********], host *********, MAC *****************."

SecretsPiiExtractor: AWS access key identifiers, GitHub tokens, JWT candidates, and URL credentials. Token boundaries use Unicode letters and digits, and exclude adjoining underscores. URL schemes start with an ASCII letter and may include digits, plus signs, hyphens and dots. Usernames and passwords must be non-empty; percent escapes require two hexadecimal digits and remain encoded in the normalized value. Host validity and scheme-specific rules are not checked.
Document credentials = new PiiAnnotator(PiiPacks.secrets()).annotate(Document.of( "Fetch s3://user:demo%40pass@example.invalid/model.bin")); String masked = Masker.mask(credentials, PiiAnnotator.PII, '*'); // "Fetch s3://****************@example.invalid/model.bin"
GitHub installation tokens start with ghs_ and have at least 36 body characters: ASCII letters, digits, underscores, hyphens and dots. The scanner reads the complete token without a fixed maximum length, following GitHub's matching guidance. Terminal dots are excluded as sentence punctuation. Token contents, checksums and active status are not verified. Other supported GitHub prefixes accept ASCII letters, digits and underscores, with a 255-character scanner limit. Their body minimum is 36 characters, or 82 for github_pat_. This installation-token example uses synthetic signature bytes:
String installationToken = "ghs_12345_eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.e30." + "A-_".repeat(160); Document credentials = new PiiAnnotator(PiiPacks.secrets()).annotate( Document.of("Bearer " + installationToken)); String masked = Masker.mask(credentials, PiiAnnotator.PII, '*'); // "Bearer " + "*".repeat(installationToken.length())
JWT detection requires three non-empty, unpadded base64url segments with valid lengths and zero unused bits. The complete UTF-8 header must be a JSON object with one top-level alg member containing a non-empty ASCII string. Member order, JSON whitespace, escaped names and nested values are supported. Detection does not verify signatures, claims or other JOSE parameter semantics. Unsigned tokens with empty signatures and five-part encrypted tokens are excluded. This example uses synthetic signature bytes, not a signed credential:
String token = "eyAiYWxnIjogIkhTMjU2IiB9.e30.dGVzdA"; Document bearer = new PiiAnnotator(PiiPacks.secrets()).annotate(Document.of("Bearer " + token)); String masked = Masker.mask(bearer, PiiAnnotator.PII, '*'); // "Bearer " + "*".repeat(token.length())

BankingPiiExtractor: 9 contiguous ASCII digits with a valid checksum and a prefix in 00-12, 21-32, 61-72 or 80, as allocated by the ABA routing policy. The 00 range includes U.S. government checks. All-zero values and digits separated by spaces or hyphens are rejected. A match does not verify that a number is assigned to an institution.

UsIdentityPiiExtractor: United States Social Security and taxpayer number candidates in 3-2-4 digit groups. The detector checks number ranges. Social Security numbers require a final group from 0001 to 9999; ITINs permit 0000 to 9999, as specified in IRS Publication 4164, table 13-16. It requires matching single ASCII spaces or hyphens; compact digits and other separators are rejected. This example masks a grouped ITIN:
Document taxpayer = new PiiAnnotator(PiiPacks.usIdentity()) .annotate(Document.of("Tax ID 900-50-0000.")); String masked = Masker.mask(taxpayer, PiiAnnotator.PII, '*'); // "Tax ID ***********."

EuIdentityPiiExtractor: United Kingdom NHS numbers and German tax identifiers. It accepts compact ASCII digits or the 3-3-4 NHS and 2-3-3-3 tax identifier groupings. Groups require matching single ASCII spaces or hyphens. Control characters, mixed delimiters and other separators are rejected. Both types require valid check digits; German identifiers also have digit-repetition checks. Uniform NHS digit runs are rejected.

CaIdentityPiiExtractor: labeled Canadian Social Insurance Number candidates. Canadian SINs require SIN, Social Insurance Number or Social Insurance No. immediately before the value. They accept 9 ASCII digits, compact or in three groups of three with matching single spaces or hyphens. Partial groupings are rejected.
DevicePiiExtractor: 15-digit, Luhn-valid IMEIs that directly follow an IMEI label. Variable-length digit groups may use single spaces or hyphens, but not a mixture of both.

section.para: Custom extractors must return a non-null list with non-null mentions inside the input text. CompositePiiExtractor and PiiAnnotator reject invalid results with IllegalArgumentException. Overlapping results are accepted. Exceptions raised by an extractor propagate unchanged.

section.title: Pseudonymizing, tokenizing, and auditing
section.para: Text replacement requires non-overlapping mentions. Pseudonymizer and HmacTokenizer.rewrite reject overlapping spans with IllegalArgumentException. Use Masker to redact combined spans without selecting a subset. HmacTokenizer.token can tokenize retained mentions individually, and audit reports accept overlapping detections.

mapSpan expands a non-empty span intersecting a replacement to include its complete label. Empty spans remain empty at their mapped position. remap omits empty annotations and changes only the spans of positional annotations. Their values are copied unchanged, including any original text or offsets in those values. Build a new PII layer from rewrite.mentions(), as above, to store the labels instead of the original values.

Document-taking rewrite and audit methods require matching annotation and PII mention offsets. They reject a mismatch with IllegalArgumentException. A custom layer must use offsets from the document text in both locations.

The default token contains sixteen hexadecimal digits (64 bits). The constructor accepts lengths from 4 to 64 digits; shorter tokens increase collision risk. Types and normalized values must contain well-formed UTF-16. Unpaired surrogates cause IllegalArgumentException in tokenization, rewriting and sampled audit values, instead of being replaced during UTF-8 encoding. Count-only reports do not encode values.

section.title: Reference data
section.para: The generators validate downloaded data before replacing Java tables. The IANA list must have a 10-digit version, a valid UTC timestamp, and at least 1,000 sorted, distinct ASCII labels. SWIFT input accepts UTF-8, Windows-1252, or UTF-16 with a byte-order mark. Its country and length rows must each occur once, have matching columns, and contain at least 80 distinct countries in alphabetical order. Lengths use two ASCII digits, from 15 through 34. Invalid input leaves the source file unchanged.

Use saved IANA or SWIFT files without downloading another copy:
IANA_TLDS_SOURCE=/path/to/tlds-alpha-by-domain.txt \ bash dev/fetch-iana-tlds.sh --check
IBAN_REGISTRY_SOURCE=/path/to/iban-registry.txt \ bash dev/fetch-iban-lengths.sh --check

Phone-table generation reads national lengths from libphonenumber metadata. Each value contains comma-separated numbers or inclusive ranges such as [8-10],12. Duplicate lengths within one value, invalid syntax, and lengths outside 1 through 31 stop generation without replacing the Java source. Ranges must contain at least three lengths; use 8,9 for a pair. Lengths shared by different phone types or territories are combined. Local-only lengths are excluded. The scanner also applies its 15-digit international-number limit. The bundled snapshot accepts national lengths 7 or 9 under +220 and 7, 9 or 10 under +263. These length checks do not confirm that a particular phone number exists.

To regenerate from a saved metadata file, provide its Git revision and commit date. The revision must contain 7 to 40 lowercase hexadecimal characters and the date must use YYYY-MM-DD with a valid calendar date. Calling codes use one to three digits without leading zeros. With --check, a difference returns a nonzero exit status and leaves the source file unchanged. This command requires Bash and JDK 21 or newer, and does not download metadata:
PHONE_METADATA_SOURCE=/path/to/PhoneNumberMetadata.xml \ PHONE_METADATA_REVISION=4ad67e90c65e365658ff9a480d3ac29ccfc6977b \ PHONE_METADATA_DATE=2026-08-28 \ bash dev/fetch-phone-number-lengths.sh --check

Run mvn -pl pii -am test -Dopennlp.forkCount=1 "-Dtest=ReferenceDataGenerator*Test" -Dsurefire.failIfNoSpecifiedTests=false to check all three generators with synthetic inputs in temporary directories. These tests require no downloaded files and run in CI when a generator, its tests, a reference table or the reference-data workflow changes. Scheduled and manual drift checks compare against live sources.
